import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-! # Woodall Primes

References:
* [Wikipedia/Woodall Number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodall_number#Woodall_primes)
* [A2234](https://oeis.org/A2234)

-/

namespace WoodallPrimes

/-- There are infinitely many prime numbers of the form `k * 2 ^ k - 1` for `k > 1`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem infinitely_many_woodall_primes : {k : ℕ | 1 < k ∧ (k * 2 ^ k - 1).Prime}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end WoodallPrimes

reformulations.difference: Lean asserts infinitude of indices k > 1 producing primes, rather than infinitude of the distinct Woodall prime values at positive indices.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The function f(k) = k * 2^k - 1 is strictly increasing on ℕ, hence injective. Its image on the set of prime-producing indices is exactly the set of Woodall primes, so the two sets are infinite simultaneously. The restriction k > 1 excludes no prime-producing index: Lean gives f(0) = 0 and f(1) = 1, neither prime. Natural subtraction agrees with integer subtraction for every positive index. These facts and the precise infinitude equivalence were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean; the proofs do not depend on sorryAx or the conjecture's proof.
